# Rules

The rules this repository enforces. Each one is a file in `.leo/rules/`, each
carries a shell command under `## Verify`, and `leo check` runs every one of
them before anything else — they are the cheapest check there is and they keep
working long after the person who learned the lesson has gone.

A rule is written **after a real bug**, never in advance. A rule with no
incident behind it is a preference, and preferences belong in a linter.

<!-- leo:rules begin -->
<!-- Generated by `leo docs --write`. Do not edit: run it again. -->

- **ADAPTER-CONTRACT** — MUST NOT add an integration that does not answer the contract
  `.leo/rules/ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md`
- **ALWAYS-LOADED** — MUST NOT grow what loads on every request
  `.leo/rules/ALWAYS-LOADED.md`
- **ASSET-SEAM** — MUST NOT read leo's own install outside the asset seam
  `.leo/rules/ASSET-SEAM.md`
- **COMMANDS-DOCUMENTED** — MUST NOT ship a command that the docs do not mention
  `.leo/rules/COMMANDS-DOCUMENTED.md`
- **FLOW-DOCUMENTED** — MUST NOT let a stage exist that the workflow does not name
  `.leo/rules/FLOW-DOCUMENTED.md`
- **ONE-EXIT-TRAP** — MUST NOT install an exit handler outside src/lib/exit.js
  `.leo/rules/ONE-EXIT-TRAP.md`
- **REVIEW-TRACKED** — MUST NOT gitignore the reviews
  `.leo/rules/REVIEW-TRACKED.md`
- **REVIEW-VOCAB** — MUST NOT let the review vocabulary drift between the file and the code
  `.leo/rules/REVIEW-VOCAB.md`
- **SKILLS-REACHABLE** — MUST NOT ship a skill the agent's runtime cannot see
  `.leo/rules/SKILLS-REACHABLE.md`
- **TOOL-DOC** — MUST NOT name a capability with no instruction file
  `.leo/rules/TOOL-DOC.md`

<!-- leo:rules end -->

## Writing one

    cp .leo/rules/EXAMPLE.md .leo/rules/MY-RULE.md

Three things, in this order:

1. **The MUST or MUST NOT**, stated so precisely that the check below is
   obvious once you have read it.
2. **Learned from** — the bug, PR or incident. If you cannot name one, you do
   not have a rule yet.
3. **A `## Verify` block** — a shell command that exits 0 when the rule holds
   and non-zero when it is violated. It runs from the repository root, it must
   be fast, and a human must be able to paste it into a terminal.

A rule that cannot be checked by a command is a line in `AGENTS.md` or
`ARCHITECTURE.md` instead. Both are fine places to be; neither is a rule.
